calibration.noChannels: Connect a micro:bit first so I know what to calibrate.
calibration.prepare: Prepare a known reference for {{name}} (e.g., a reference standard or table value).
calibration.sending: Sending calibration for {{name}}, waiting for reply…
calibration.tipDistance1: Measure a known distance with a ruler and ensure the sensor points perpendicular to the target.
calibration.tipForce1: Hang a known weight (e.g., 1 N = 100 g) from the load cell hook.
calibration.tipForce2: Keep the load cell vertical and motionless.
calibration.tipGeneric: Prepare a reference value you know with adequate precision.
calibration.tipPressure1: Use the local atmospheric pressure from a meteorological service for your altitude.
calibration.tipPressure2: For hydrostatic calibration, measure the water column height above the sensor.
calibration.tipTemperature1: Use a verified thermometer or a known fixed point (ice melt = 0 °C, water boiling = 100 °C).
calibration.tipTemperature2: Let the sensor equilibrate in the medium for at least 30 s before entering the reference value.
calibration.title: Sensor calibration
calibration.valueHelp: Use a decimal point. The value is sent to the micro:bit which computes a new calibration factor.
calibration.warningFactor: Warning: the new factor is far outside the usual range. Double-check the entered value and sensor wiring.

connection.bluetoothHint: No cable, works on tablets and phones · micro:bit V2 only
connection.firmwareHint: Once is enough. One file for V1 and V2 — the board picks its own half, and Bluetooth only switches on for V2.
connection.guideLink: Not sure how to wire the sensor? Open the guide →
connection.insecureContext: Connecting to a micro:bit only works over https:// or on localhost. This page is served over an insecure connection, so the browser blocked device access. Open the app at https://fyzbit.cz/.
connection.serialHint: Web Serial · works in Chrome / Edge on Windows, macOS and Linux.
connection.stepFirmware: Flash the firmware onto the micro:bit
connection.title: Connect micro:bit
connection.unsupportedBluetooth: This browser has no Web Bluetooth. Chrome or Edge on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and ChromeOS work; Firefox and Safari (including every browser on iPhone and iPad) do not implement it. On a desktop, use the USB cable.
connection.unsupportedSerial: This browser has no Web Serial, so connecting over a USB cable is not possible. Chrome, Edge or Opera on a desktop work; Firefox and Safari do not implement it. On a tablet or phone, choose Bluetooth.
connection.unsupportedUsb: This browser has no WebUSB, so the firmware cannot be flashed from here. Download the .hex file below and drop it onto the MICROBIT drive that appears when you plug the board in.

error.browserUnsupported: This browser has neither Web Serial nor Web Bluetooth, so it cannot connect to a micro:bit. Chrome, Edge and Opera work; Firefox and Safari (and every browser on iPhone and iPad) do not implement them. You can still try the app in demo mode with a simulated sensor.
error.calibrationTimeout: Calibration did not respond. Try again.
error.insecureContext: This page is not served over a secure connection (https), so the browser blocked access to the micro:bit. Open the app at https://fyzbit.cz/.
error.noHandshake: The board did not introduce itself. Press both buttons A+B on the micro:bit, or unplug it and connect again.
error.sensorReadFailed: The sensor could not be read — check the wiring. Over Bluetooth the radio interferes with the DS18B20 thermometer; over the cable it reads reliably.
error.storageSaveFailed: Auto-save is failing (full storage or private browsing mode) — the current recording is not being saved.

wiring.boardCredit: Board drawing © Micro:bit Educational Foundation · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
wiring.noteDs18b20: A 4.7 kΩ resistor belongs between DATA and VCC — without it the probe returns nothing.
wiring.noteHcsr04: Some HC-SR04 units want 5 V. If nothing reads on 3V, power the module from 5 V.
wiring.noteHx710b: Attach the tubing after wiring, so no pressure is left trapped in the sensor.
wiring.noteHx711: The load cell solders to E+, E−, A+, A− on the other side of the module.
wiring.photoDs18b20: DS18B20 probe — a stainless steel tip on a long cable ending in three crocodile clips.
wiring.photoHcsr04: HC-SR04 module — a blue board with two silver ultrasonic transducers.
wiring.photoHx710b: Board carrying the pressure sensor with its hose nipple, and the converter.
wiring.photoHx711: Aluminium load cell beam with a hanging eyelet, in an enclosure with the converter.
